statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk of 18% sits in the low band, below the 20% watch threshold and well below the 25% block level.
recommendation: Tail remains below both the watch and block thresholds. The Nasdaq-100 has held a defined 31,208-31,361 range for several hours after setting a record high, the retracement off that high was granted and has held, and VIX and the 10-year yield are both near session lows, so the observed structure is an orderly uptrend in which mean reversion is functioning. Stress stays elevated at 47% on the 30-year yield near its 2002 highs, Brent above $100, record three-stock index concentration and a Russell 2000 diverging from the index, but none of that has produced the shallow-pullback, failed-retracement signature that defines Tail. The narrow danger window is limited to the 10-year note auction and FOMC minutes block between 17:00Z and 19:00Z on 7 October. Mapped policy state: EA_ON.
headline: Nasdaq-100 holds a defined range 0.28% below today's record high into the closing auction as VIX and the 10-year yield sit at session lows; Tail 18% with the FOMC minutes block the next checkpoint
body: The Nasdaq-100 trades at 31,274.04 (+197.59, +0.64%) in the final hour of US cash trade, about 0.28% below the 31,361.37 record high set earlier today, which is also the new 52-week high. The session range is 31,208.20-31,361.37 and price has now spent several hours oscillating inside it instead of extending, which is direct evidence that retracements are being granted rather than failing. The session low held 0.42% above Monday's 31,076.44 record close, so the gap above the prior record is unfilled and the uptrend is structurally intact. December NQ futures tell the same story at 31,520.50 (+0.65%), roughly 0.30% below their own 31,616.50 session high inside a 31,309.25-31,616.50 range. Cross-asset evidence is de-amplifying rather than confirming a pathological path. VIX is 15.06 (-2.96%) against a 14.96-15.54 range and a 15.52 previous close, sitting close to its session low. The 10-year yield has eased four basis points to 5.27% and trades at the bottom of a 5.26-5.30% range after Monday's 5.31% multi-decade high. The latest H.15 reading, for October 2, put the 2-year constant-maturity yield at 4.83%, the 10-year at 5.28% and the 30-year at 5.63%; the 30-year is now near 5.64%, still close to its 2002 highs, which is the main standing reason Stress stays elevated while Tail does not. Semiconductors are aligned with the index rather than leading it away: the SOX is 13,250.10 (+0.59%) and about 0.75% below its own 13,349.96 session high, so the sector pulled back with the index. Leadership remains narrow. The Russell 2000 is down 0.56% at 2,831.29 against the Nasdaq-100's gain, and Nvidia, Apple and Microsoft together now exceed 21% of the S&P 500, an unprecedented three-stock concentration that leaves the benchmark dependent on very few names. Nvidia reached fresh highs with an intraday market capitalisation of about $5.84 trillion on continued AI infrastructure demand, Marvell gained roughly 8% after raising fiscal 2028 guidance to about $20 billion, and Constellation Energy rose about 13% on a $4.3 billion nuclear supply agreement with Google. Energy is the clearest conflicting input: WTI is $89.62 (+0.21%) after trading below $87 earlier in the session, and Brent is $100.79 (+0.47%), so crude is elevated with a wide two-way range rather than breaking out. Taken together the observed picture is an orderly uptrend near record levels in which mean reversion is working, with an elevated long-end yield and energy backdrop that supports Stress but not Tail. The shared Finviz context file was last collected on 2026-09-29 and is therefore far outside its 90-minute freshness contract, so it was not used; the assessment rests entirely on independently verified current sources, and Confidence is scored on that evidence. The forward window carries two genuine scheduled checkpoints: the 10-year note auction at 17:00Z on 7 October, which matters because the long end has only just eased, and the FOMC minutes at 18:00Z, a structurally multi-stage event whose headline read, yield reaction and delayed equity second leg can separate. Those two hours define the narrow danger window. Mapped policy state: EA_ON, with forecast Tail peaking at 23% in the minutes hour, which remains inside the watch band and below the 25% block threshold.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. Tail ran 20% at 19:00Z on 5 October, fell through the overnight hours to a low of 8% at 05:00Z as the index mean-reverted in thin liquidity, then rebuilt with the European and US sessions to a 22% peak at 15:00Z on 6 October around the record-high push. The last two hours settled back to 17% as the retracement off the high was granted and held. Dominant mode moved from trend-up to mixed overnight and back to trend-up from 10:00Z. Stress stayed in the elevated band throughout, between 45% and 54%, and Confidence held in the high band between 86% and 88%.
outlookSummary: Tail is expected to ease through the US close and the Asian session as liquidity thins and the closing auction completes, reaching a 10% area between 01:00Z and 05:00Z. It rebuilds with the European open and the US pre-market, then rises into the 7 October US session: 19% for the cash-open hour at 13:00Z, 21% for the first full post-open hour and the Consumer Inflation Expectations hour, and a 23% peak in the 18:00Z FOMC minutes hour. That peak stays inside the watch band and below the 25% block threshold because no pathological price path is observed; it reflects the aligned catalyst stack of a 10-year auction and multi-stage minutes landing with the long end near multi-decade highs. Stress follows the same arc from 45% overnight to 52% at the minutes, and Confidence decays from 87% to 81% as live cash evidence ages.
